answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: each agent identity earns a rolling reputation thread from its actions over prior epochs, and every new epoch must reconcile with that history. An identity rising toward the summit of trust must show continuous, coherent behaviour; sudden capability jumps or dormancy gaps cap its score. Enforcement costs an attacker one consistent operating history per identity, sustained across epochs. Splitting into many identities raises costs linearly, like a rising tide of maintenance overhead that never amortizes, so fake identities gain no leverage.
